name: Saraiki
notes:
Saraiki (سرائیکی) written in the Saraiki Shahmukhi alphabet standardised by the Anjuman Taraqqi-e-Saraiki, an extension of the Urdu Perso-Arabic abjad. Its defining typological feature is the implosive series, and the standard assigns each implosive a dedicated letter: ٻ /ɓ/, ڄ /ʄ/, ݙ /ɗ/, ڳ /ɠ/ (Shackle 1976; Bashir & Conners 2019). The implosive dal is ݙ (U+0759, dal with two dots below and small tah), not the Sindhi ڏ (U+068F); the retroflex nasal /ɳ/ likewise has its own letter ݨ (U+0768, noon with small tah), which carries the productive infinitive suffix -ݨ and is one of the commonest letters in the language.

The rhotic ر is a tap /ɾ/, contrasting with the retroflex flap ڑ /ɽ/ (Bashir & Conners 2019); و is the labiodental /v/ named in the language's attested inventory (PHOIBLE, sera1259). Nasals assimilate in place before a following stop, so ن before گ surfaces as /ŋ/.

و and ی are matres lectionis as well as glides, and position decides which. After a consonant they spell the long vowel (و = oː/uː, ی = eː/iː); word-initially, and in the second slot of a doubled mater (وو, یو), they are the glides /v/ and /j/. Word-finally ی is /iː/ and و is /uː/. Alef is the same distinction in reverse: word-initial ا is a bare carrier for an unwritten short vowel, while initial /aː/ is written with the madda, آ; elsewhere ا is /aː/. The hamza seats ئ and ؤ are orthographic supports and are normally silent.

Short vowels are not written in this abjad and gemination is not marked, so both are unrecoverable from unvowelised input; they account for the bulk of the residual distance against the WikiPron skr_arab_broad gold, which transcribes them. That gold also splits ا between aː and ɑː and the mid front long vowel between eː and ɛː; these are notation choices, not competing analyses. Saraiki word stress is not orthographically predictable and is exempt per quality_tiers.md.
